page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.2xlarge is an entry-tier burstable virtual machine from the shared server family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 8 x86_64 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES instructions. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The server includes no local disk storage, relies entirely on network-attached storage, has no hardware GPUs, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements reflect the burstable, shared-core profile of the instance. Single-thread compute falls into lower percentile tiers, with Geekbench single-core scoring 809.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 1053.09. Single-threaded gzip compression (18.94 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (6.43 GB/sec) also align with the bottom 10% of benchmarks. Multi-core performance scales moderately due to the 8 vCPUs, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 9165.89 and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 8203.45, both placing in the middle 50% category. In application-specific suites, Geekbench clang software compilation achieves 7053.0, while Redis SET operations handle 8.4 million operations per second.

Memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate 519.54 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached blocks, decreasing to 57.64 GB/sec read and 45.1 GB/sec write on uncached 256 MB blocks. However, the overall PassMark memory score of 1375.33 and database operations mark of 1833.86 sit in the bottom 25%, constrained by the limited 8.0 GB capacity across 8 vCPUs. Static web serving throughput reaches 4.84 GB/sec. Small 135M parameter LLM inference achieves 374.7 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 75.88 tokens/sec for text generation, while 7B and 70B models cannot run due to memory limitations.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the low memory-to-core ratio paired with burstable CPU limits, which introduces performance throttling under sustained saturation. Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.2xlarge is economically matched for intermittent workloads that benefit from multi-threaded execution without continuous peak CPU or heavy memory requirements, such as periodic code compilation, lightweight microservices, testing environments, and low-traffic staging systems.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.2xlarge is a burstable, shared-core instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a lean 1:1 memory-to-core allocation of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance includes 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, no dedicated GPUs, and zero local storage, relying on external storage volumes. Benchmark data indicates modest single-thread capabilities, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 809.0, alongside moderate multi-threaded capacity including a PassMark CPU score of 9165.89 and 8.4 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory constraints limit large model execution and intensive database tasks, making the instance primarily suitable for bursty compute, lightweight application testing, low-traffic background processing, and intermittent batch compilation tasks.
